The '''2014–15 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 113th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 83rd in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the fifth since its organization under a league committee separate from [[Serie B]]. It began on 30 August 2014.

A total of 20 teams competed in the league: 17 sides from the [[2013–14 Serie A|2013–14 season]] and three promoted from the [[2013–14 Serie B]] campaign. [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] were the defending champions, successfully defending their title for the fourth consecutive time. On 2 May 2015, Juventus won the ''Scudetto'' for the fourth consecutive time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/juventus/story/2428648/juventus-win-fourth-straight-serie-a-title-at-sampdoria|title=Juventus win fourth straight Serie A title with away victory at Sampdoria|date=2 May 2015|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref>

==Events==
[[File:Juventus line-up vs Malmoe 2014.jpg|thumb|200px|right|2014–15 Juventus team]]
The season featured the return of [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]] after only one season in the second division and [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]], whose last appearance was in the [[2007–08 Serie A|2007–08]] season. [[A.C. Cesena|Cesena]], the play-off winner, returned to the top level after two years in Serie B.

The pre-season saw two ownership changes: [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] was sold from [[Massimo Cellino]] to Milanese entrepreneur Tommaso Giulini, a former board member at [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]]. [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] was sold by Edoardo Garrone (son of the late [[Riccardo Garrone (entrepreneur)|Riccardo Garrone]]) to Rome-based film businessman Massimo Ferrero.

The season was also influenced by serious financial problems surrounding [[Parma F.C.|Parma]], involving two controversial takeovers during the season, its last chairman Giampietro Manenti being arrested on 18 March 2015 under accusation of money laundering, and the club being ultimately declared insolvent by the local court on the very next day.

The Serie A this season had the most goals on average than any of the five other top leagues in Europe.<ref>https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/blogs/world-of-sport/1024-goals--serie-a-was-the-highest-scoring-league-in-europe-this-season-090941358.html {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref>
